statement: Find all positive integers with two or more digits such that inserting a 0 between the units and tens digits gives a multiple of the original number.

\(A, B, C\) are collinear with \(B\) between \(A\) and \(C\). \(K_1\) has diameter \(AB\), \(K_2\) has diameter \(BC\). Another circle touches \(AC\) at \(B\) and meets \(K_1\) again at \(P\) and \(K_2\) again at \(Q\). Line \(PQ\) meets \(K_1\) again at \(R\) and \(K_2\) again at \(S\). Show that \(AR\) and \(CS\) meet on the perpendicular to \(AC\) at \(B\).

At a party there are \(n\) women and \(n\) men. Each woman likes \(r\) of the men, and each man likes \(s\) of the women. For which \(r\) and \(s\) must there be a man and a woman who like each other?

Quadrilateral \(ABCD\) has \(AB \parallel CD\). \(P\) on \(AB\) and \(Q\) on \(CD\) satisfy \(\frac{PA}{PB} = \frac{DQ}{CQ}\). \(M\) is the intersection of \(AQ\) and \(DP\), and \(N\) of \(PC\) and \(QB\). Find \(MN\) in terms of \(AB\) and \(CD\).

There is one card for each pair \((a, b)\) with \(1 \leq a < b \leq 2003\). Two players alternately remove a card and write \(ab\) on the blackboard. The first player who causes the \(\gcd\) of all numbers on the board to equal 1 loses. Which player has a winning strategy?

Given a positive integer \(n\), allowed moves are to form \(2n+1\) or \(3n+2\). The set \(S_n\) contains all numbers reachable from \(n\). Call \(m\) and \(n\) compatible if \(S_m \cap S_n \neq \emptyset\). Which members of \(\{1, 2, 3, \ldots, 2002\}\) are compatible with 2003?
